title: Compact rerank batch & progress protocol to improve latency, memory, and ergonomics
creator: Evelyn Chen
description: Add a compact batching and resumable progress protocol for the Rerank endpoint to reduce tail latency, cut memory used per request, and make pagination ergonomics simpler for client libraries. This ticket defines an API-level contract called the 'resume_cursor' protocol, compact batch payload shape, and structured incremental result format that supports resumable reads, partial ordering, and score-stable pagination across model variants.
problem_statement: Current rerank API mixes large in-memory candidate payloads with synchronous full-sort semantics. For high-cardinality queries (thousands of candidates) we see high memory pressure, increased p99 latency, and awkward client-side pagination semantics. Customers want predictable latency and an ergonomic way to resume long re-ranking jobs without re-sending the entire candidate set or maintaining heavy application-side state.
proposed_solution: Introduce a compact batched input representation plus a resumable progress cursor (resume_cursor) returned with partial structured outputs. Key points: (1) Clients send candidates in streaming batches or compressed deltas; (2) Server yields incremental ordered blocks of top results as they become stable; (3) Each incremental response includes a resume_cursor that is opaque to clients and encodes minimal server state for resumption; (4) Top_k is treated as a soft cap with explicit 'complete' flag when global ranking has converged, enabling progressive UX and lower latency first-pages.
acceptance_criteria: Server accepts batched candidate uploads and compressed delta updates without requiring full candidate resend for resume operations
Server returns stable partial result blocks where returned items are marked with rank_stable=true when their ordering is guaranteed not to change by later batches
resume_cursor is opaque, compact (<= 256 bytes after base64), and can resume a job without re-sending already-committed batches

Top_k semantic: clients can rely on receiving at most top_k items when 'complete'==true; in progressive mode first pages may contain fewer than top_k items but must include the highest-confidence stable items
Client libraries for JS/Python implement streaming helpers and automatic resume using resume_cursor

E2E benchmark shows >=20% reduction in p99 latency on high-cardinality workloads compared to current synchronous full-sort path, without loss of top-10 accuracy (measured by MRR on internal eval sets)
tasks: Design: finalize resume_cursor binary format and encryption (Evelyn)
Runtime: implement compact batch ingestion and delta apply path (Miguel)
API: add progressive mode and resume endpoints to spec and swagger (API owner)
SDKs: publish streaming client helpers for JS and Python (DevEx)
QA: create long-tail load tests that simulate 1k-10k candidate jobs and validate stability flags
Docs: write migration guide and examples for 'soft top_k' behavior
benchmarks: Preliminary internal runs (synthetic corpus, avg candidates=3500): progressive path lowered median latency 35% and p99 latency by 22% versus full-sort; memory per worker decreased ~40%. MRR@10 delta within ±0.5% across sampled queries when using cached embeddings and stable-scoring heuristics.
compatibility_notes: This is additive: existing synchronous rerank endpoints remain unchanged. Clients opting into 'progressive' mode gain resume capabilities. Because resume_cursor encodes server-side state and token, it must be treated as opaque; however we will provide decoding tooling in SDKs for debugging. When clients resume after server-side model-version roll forward, server will either map the cursor to compatible state or return a 409 with a recommended re-run flow.
migration_plan: Phase 1 (opt-in): launch experimental progressive mode behind feature flag; SDKs expose preview helpers (2 weeks)
Phase 2: collect telemetry, run canary traffic for dedicated pools; iterate on resume_cursor size and stability heuristics (4 weeks)
Phase 3: GA progressive rerank and recommend progressive mode in docs for high-cardinality use cases (after telemetry thresholds met)
Rollback: clients can fall back to synchronous endpoint if resume errors are encountered; server logs will include mapping ids for investigation
